name: REA Reverse Engineering
description: Connect Astravia to REA so the agent can reverse engineer native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, firmware and website traffic — with evidence for every conclusion.
setup.title: REA setup
setup.subtitle: Astravia provisions the official rea-agents CLI on first use and verifies it through a probe. Once the status reads Ready, the agent can call REA tools in conversations.
setup.step1: Probe whether the official rea-agents CLI is already installed.
setup.step2: Install the official rea-agents CLI from npm if the probe is missing or stale.
setup.step3: Verify the CLI responds to --version and reports a working environment.
setup.step4: REA tools are now available to the agent through the bundled skill.
setup.stepCliDescription: Astravia only installs the official npm package when the CLI is missing. It does not add another Astravia tool or modify your global PATH.
setup.stepCliBusy: Astravia is currently probing the CLI. This may take up to a minute while npx fetches the package on first use.
setup.stepCliError: The probe could not reach the REA CLI. You can retry the setup or run `npx rea-agents doctor --json` from a terminal for diagnostics.
setup.stepReadyTitle: CLI is ready for the agent
setup.stepReadyDescription: The agent can now invoke REA tools and follow the bundled reverse-engineer-anything skill workflow.
setup.doctorHint: Run `npx rea-agents doctor --json` from a terminal for a structured diagnostic report.

tab.detail.connect.heading: Only connect when you need to
tab.detail.connect.subtitle: First check whether REA is already registered and not stale, then decide whether setup is needed. Installing this skill does not register the MCP server.
tab.detail.connect.bullet1: Use what already works: when REA tools are registered and not stale, call them directly and skip doctor or setup.
tab.detail.connect.bullet2: Run doctor to distinguish three failure shapes: missing registration, session that needs a restart, or a missing provider.
tab.detail.connect.bullet3: Dry-run before any configuration change: let the official setup print the paths, backups and skill replacement it intends to write.
tab.detail.connect.bullet4: REA setup never installs Node, npm, Java, Ghidra, IDA, JADX, Binwalk or Unblob — those must already exist.
tab.detail.connect.diagramAria: Connect decision tree: doctor → three failure shapes → dry-run → next stage.
tab.detail.connect.fallback: If doctor still fails, return to the user's original request and do whatever is supported, then come back once REA is repaired.
tab.detail.route.heading: Pick the first tool from the target
tab.detail.route.subtitle: Choose the entry MCP tool based on the user-supplied target. Target-free tools take their own path or endpoint directly.
tab.detail.route.bullet1: ASAR or JS tree: analyze_javascript_application. Archive inventory: open_binary, then inspect_artifact when the graph helps.
tab.detail.route.bullet2: Android: inspect_android_package. Managed: inspect_managed_artifact. Firmware: inspect_firmware_regions, then extract_firmware on demand.
tab.detail.route.bullet3: Browser / Electron: list_browser_targets, list_electron_targets. Check inspect_electron_fuses before attempting an electron-main Inspector.
tab.detail.route.bullet4: Packet capture / signal recordings: inspect_packet_capture, decode_signal_recording. Inspect decoder and protocol first, then apply filters.
tab.detail.route.diagramAria: Route fan-out: 22 target types split into four evidence buckets, then pick a mode.
tab.detail.route.fallback: When the user only says 'my app', ask for the name or path. Never pick a sample app on their behalf.
tab.detail.summary.heading: Work summary-first
tab.detail.summary.subtitle: For large targets, use detail: summary to fetch the overview, then page through parent_evidence_id instead of returning the whole result in one frame.
tab.detail.summary.bullet1: Unknown-size JS or ELF targets: analyze_javascript_application or inspect_binary_layout with detail: summary first.
tab.detail.summary.bullet2: Page with inspect_analysis_view using the parent_evidence_id from the previous result.
tab.detail.summary.bullet3: When transport reports resource_constraint, do not rerun the large call — switch to summary, a single section, or a stable page.
tab.detail.summary.bullet4: Treat client-truncated output as incomplete. When the full record is needed, use export_evidence_bundle to write it to a chosen path.
tab.detail.summary.diagramAria: Five-field summary report: who, where, what, why, evidence.
tab.detail.summary.fallback: Evidence is always retained. If the parent ID is unknown, look it up with get_evidence_bundle and explicit filters.
tab.detail.plan.heading: Plan broader investigations
tab.detail.plan.subtitle: Multi-feature requests follow a seven-step rhythm: checklist, reuse, smallest useful overview, related resources, multiple evidence types, parallel workers, concise ledger.
tab.detail.plan.bullet1: Turn the request into a checklist of questions and the evidence each answer needs before asking again.
tab.detail.plan.bullet2: Reuse the current REA session, artifact, saved analysis database, bookmarks and prior evidence. Do not open a duplicate session.
tab.detail.plan.bullet3: Corroborate each conclusion with the evidence type it requires. Use runtime observation only when static evidence cannot answer the question.
tab.detail.plan.bullet4: Keep a concise finding ledger linking each conclusion to its Evidence ID, confidence, search boundary and remaining unknowns.
tab.detail.plan.diagramAria: Plan eight-step loop: five core steps, one checkpoint, one summary, one restart.
tab.detail.plan.fallback: Before finishing, revisit the original checklist. Mark each question answered, partially answered or unresolved, and do not declare the investigation complete while required questions remain open.
tab.detail.read.heading: Read only the relevant guide
tab.detail.read.subtitle: The upstream SKILL.md links to five references. Pick the one that matches the target type. Paths are relative to the reverse-engineer-anything skill directory.
tab.detail.read.bullet1: Native binaries, managed assemblies, archives and extraction: references/native-and-artifacts.md.
tab.detail.read.bullet2: ASARs, JS trees, feature tracing and version comparison: references/javascript-applications.md.
tab.detail.read.bullet3: Android APK declarations, classes, methods and references: references/android-applications.md. Browser / Electron observation: references/runtime-observation.md.
tab.detail.read.bullet4: Evidence paging, comparisons, residual unknowns and verification: references/evidence-workflows.md.
tab.detail.read.diagramAria: Read routing: summary → six reference files matched to the target type.
tab.detail.read.fallback: When unsure which guide to read, pull a summary with inspect_analysis_view first, then jump to the matching section in the references.
tab.detail.finish.heading: Finish the task
tab.detail.finish.subtitle: Explain findings in plain language, tie each conclusion to its evidence, preserve limitations and unknowns, and never let static analysis pretend to be runtime observation.
tab.detail.finish.bullet1: Explain the conclusion in plain language and bring the user back to the original question. Do not paste evidence JSON on its own.
tab.detail.finish.bullet2: When the user wants to rebuild or modify something, switch back to normal coding tools and use the reverse-engineering result as input, not as the code itself.
tab.detail.finish.bullet3: For runtime requests, only act on the declared target and lifecycle. Do not broaden the target or the action beyond what was requested.
tab.detail.finish.bullet4: Before finishing, export_evidence_bundle to write the complete investigation to a user-selected directory for replay and review.
tab.detail.finish.diagramAria: Finish checklist: five deliverables before declaring the investigation complete.
tab.detail.finish.fallback: When a phenomenon is genuinely unknown, 'unknown' is a valid answer. Do not drop the evidence and the limitation just to produce an answer.
tab.detail.points.waiting: Lights up as the conversation progresses; nothing is marked done without a signal
tab.detail.connect.point1.detail: An entry tool such as open_binary / binary_session returned successfully, so the engine can open this target.
tab.detail.connect.point2.detail: doctor actually ran in this conversation and no check failed.
tab.detail.connect.point3.detail: A setup dry run lists the paths and backups it would write; nothing is written without your approval.
tab.detail.connect.point4.detail: Missing registration, a stale session, and an uninstalled provider are three different problems with different fixes.
tab.detail.route.point1.detail: A JavaScript / Electron tool ran, so the target counts as JavaScript.
tab.detail.route.point2.detail: The first mobile, .NET, or firmware tool is what settles the type.
tab.detail.route.point3.detail: Listing browser / Electron targets or reading fuses separates an Electron app from plain JS.
tab.detail.route.point4.detail: Capture and signal tools appearing means this target has a network or runtime component.
tab.detail.summary.point1.detail: Who / where / what / why can only be summarised after some stage tool has run.
tab.detail.summary.point2.detail: Reading the summary through inspect_analysis_view is what actually hands the ledger to you.
tab.detail.summary.point3.detail: When static evidence is thin, runtime observation fills in the same conclusion.
tab.detail.summary.point4.detail: Only after an evidence bundle export can the investigation be replayed and audited.
tab.detail.plan.point1.detail: Once both planning and guide-reading have run, the checklist is actually being executed.
tab.detail.plan.point2.detail: Reuse existing sessions and evidence: keep asking the old session instead of opening a second one.
tab.detail.plan.point3.detail: Tools such as correlate / compare / instrument tie multiple leads together.
tab.detail.plan.point4.detail: Writing conclusions into the ledger and flagging unknowns is how this checklist ships.
tab.detail.read.point1.detail: After opening a native or managed target, the matching reference is worth reading.
tab.detail.read.point2.detail: The JavaScript reference is only needed once ASAR / JS trees are in play.
tab.detail.read.point3.detail: Android packages and browser runtime observation are two different references.
tab.detail.read.point4.detail: The evidence-workflow reference becomes required once finish begins.
tab.detail.finish.point1.detail: Finish-stage tools actually running is the signal that conclusions are becoming deliverables.
tab.detail.finish.point2.detail: Every claim carries an Evidence ID, with observation and inference written separately.
tab.detail.finish.point3.detail: Even at runtime, only touch the target and lifecycle you declared.
tab.detail.finish.point4.detail: A successful export_evidence_bundle means the report can be replayed.

tab.diagram.finish.check5: Original checklist revisited; no open questions left unmarked.

tab.target.javascript.label: JavaScript / Electron
tab.target.javascript.hint: Static analysis of bundled JS, source maps, Electron fuses, and runtime reconciliation. Use when the artifact is a .js/.asar bundle or an Electron app.
tab.target.dotnet.label: .NET / managed
tab.target.dotnet.hint: Decompile .NET assemblies, read IL, dump dynamic types with Harmony. Use when the artifact is a .dll / .exe that loads as managed code.
tab.target.native.label: Native / artifacts
tab.target.native.hint: Disassemble native binaries with Hopper / Ghidra / IDA, instrument with Frida. Use when the binary is unmanaged (C/C++/Rust/Go).
tab.target.firmware.label: Firmware
tab.target.firmware.hint: Unpack firmware, scan with binwalk and YARA, lift code in Ghidra. Use when the input is a raw flash dump or a router/IoT image.
tab.target.web.label: Web / network
tab.target.web.hint: Capture HTTP/3 / WebSocket / TLS traffic, trace module calls in the browser, replay scenarios. Use when the target is a web app or a service API.
tab.target.mobile.label: Mobile
tab.target.mobile.hint: Decompile Android APKs (jadx / apktool), inspect iOS bundles, attach with Frida over adb. Use when the target runs on a phone or tablet.
